author: reek
body: Nothing else writes that cell. The host does not touch it and no path the boot processor can take reaches it. So a value above zero is not evidence that six processes ran -- it is evidence that a core which is not the boot processor took one out of the table and executed it. A probe that only showed six children finishing would pass exactly as happily on one core, and a test that cannot fail is how SMP came to be faked here once already.

author: reek
body: The spin is long on purpose. An idle core now halts rather than busy-scans, and rises again on a wake IPI or its timer, so it takes a millisecond or so to claim newly published work -- during which the never-halting boot processor, arriving in the dispatch loop the instant it blocks, can run a short child to completion itself. If each child finished in less than that wake latency the boot processor would take all six and no application processor would claim any, and the test would report NO AP RAN A PROCESS while dispatch worked perfectly. The child outlives the wake by a wide margin, so a core that wakes has work still waiting. This is the same reason smp-preempt spins long.
